historical_reviews.v3_1: The safety meaning of a power limit depends on enabled state, watts, correction interval, statistics period and exception action as one coherent policy tuple.

original_test_intent: Read the configured DCMI power-limit policy through the local in-band interface and verify its complete enabled/value/action/timing state without modifying it.
original_method: Retain the exact local raw 0x2c 0x03 0xdc 0 0 request and decode the whole policy response against the approved platform contract.
manual_activity: The project supplies the DCMI response schema and approved enabled/limit/action/correction/sampling policy tuple; the end user owns PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED.
safety_requirements: Do not issue Set Power Limit
No shutdown, throttle, reset or workload action
agent_execution_scope: Bind local interface to intended SUT
Decode enabled state and limit watts
Decode correction time, sampling period and exception action
engineer_actions: Provide policy schema and authoritative expected tuple

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The high-level getter may be supplemental, while SSH is unnecessary for the named local route unless runner topology is approved; its text output does not prove exact framing or reserved-field validation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: On the verified local interface, issue `ipmitool raw 0x2c 0x03 0xdc 0 0` once, preserve the complete response, decode every enabled/limit/action/timing field and compare the resulting tuple without writing.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source payload and 10/5 timing remain; no expected limit, action or interval is guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a source-exact local policy snapshot and validate it atomically as enabled state, watts, correction time, sampling period, exception action and reserved fields against an approved target-specific tuple.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds policy semantics and a fail-closed comparison beyond command completion.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Power Reading reports consumption rather than configured enforcement policy; OOB evidence does not prove the local route; setter behavior is intentionally excluded.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Mis-decoding a disabled bit or exception action can reverse the apparent safety posture even when the watt value looks correct.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish/vendor getter is equivalent only if it exposes all DCMI policy fields and maps enabled/action/timing semantics; omitted raw and in-band coverage must be disclosed.
expected_evidence: Approved response contract, decoder version and expected policy tuple
Exact raw request and complete response with completion/length
Enabled state, limit watts, correction time and sampling period
No power-policy, thermal, reset, workload, configuration or log mutation

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and raw procedure consistently describe an in-band Get Power Limit operation. The completion-only criterion is incomplete, not contradictory; the DeepSeek high-level wrapper is an overlay fidelity gap.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The getter and raw payload are explicit. Decoder semantics and the expected policy tuple are standard project readiness inputs.

review_improvement: Replaces opaque command success with an atomic, field-complete comparison of the active DCMI power-limit policy.
independent_technical_reasoning: A power limit is not a scalar setting: the same watt value has different operational meaning when the policy is disabled, uses a different correction time, averages over another sampling period, or selects a shutdown instead of a logging exception. Automation must decode and compare the tuple as a whole and refuse to repair mismatches, because a compensating write would transform this getter into a safety-sensitive setter test.
